name: no-time
title: No time to type
kicker: Why this talk · the second ground has four legs
html:
No time to type

Family, a new dog, a phone in one hand and a leash in the other. The dog sets the pace.

Safe while nobody watches

Offered only what the state allows. A refusal says why.

Cheap when repeated

Think once, then replay with no model.

Short to say

A goal in words, not a manual. One thumb’s worth.

So the agent finds its way from the answers, not from me.

/remote-control

Please give me an update

Red run logged. Writing the fix.

How’s it going?

Green. Committed through the gate.

🐕 pulling. back in 20

Illustrative, not a transcript. The two questions are the real ones, every evening. So is the dog.
say: The second ground is personal, and it has four legs. Family, and a new dog. Typing time is gone: one hand holds a leash, the other a phone. So most of my work is steered by thumb, through Claude Code's /remote-control: the session runs on my machine at home, and I answer it from the sidewalk. My prompts got very short. Most evenings it's two: 'Please give me an update', and 'How's it going?' The dog sets the pace. That changes what an agent has to be. Safe while nobody watches every step: offered only what the state allows, and a refusal that says why. Cheap when it does the same thing again: think once, replay with no model, which is Hightower's point. And short to say: a goal in words, not a manual. So the agent finds its way from the answers, not from me. Hold on to that; it's why the controls have to be in the answers.
